title: EMIs ran for a phone that never came; retailer told to pay ₹1.14 lakh

slides.head: EMIs ran for a phone that never came; retailer told to pay ₹1.14 lakh
What happened
slides.body: The commission ordered a ₹74,698 refund, ₹30,000 for mental agony and ₹10,000 litigation costs, and told the retailer to get the loan account closed.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The buyer shared an OTP in the store in March 2024 to process a zero-interest EMI purchase; the first ₹4,204 EMI was deducted on April 3, 2024, with no phone handed over.

slides.head: ordered to the buyer
slides.body: The retailer had no signed receipt, stock entry or gate pass to show the handset was handed over.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: The first EMI of ₹4,204 was deducted on April 3, 2024, with no phone in hand.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether the retailer complies or appeals; the article does not say. Ask: Who should prove a product was delivered: the buyer or the seller?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
EMIs ran for a phone that never came; retailer told to pay ₹1.14 lakh

A Hyderabad district consumer commission ordered an electronics retailer to refund ₹74,698 and pay ₹40,000 more after a buyer's zero-interest EMIs began without the phone ever being delivered.

Why it matters: The buyer shared an OTP in the store in March 2024 to process a zero-interest EMI purchase; the first ₹4,204 EMI was deducted on April 3, 2024, with no phone handed over.

Source: Siasat. Image: Siasat
